prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Offshore wind farm O&M. Out of scope: grid, port. Offshore Substation (Morrowick; Transformer Tap Snapshot→Shore Control Room; Switching Window Acknowledgment); Main Transformer (site-specific trip); export cable→Grid Interface Relay (Wildmere; Export Limit Advisory→Grid Dispatcher if capability<target; applies Dispatcher ceiling); Grid Dispatcher: requirements→Relay. Turbine: Turbine Controller (Glassfin; validated commands; Pitch Deviation Notice; safe mode on aux loss; shutdown on confirmed fire), Pitch System, Rotor Brake Unit, Converter Cabinet (isolated on fire/overheat), Nacelle Condition Monitor, Turbine Sensor Bus. Blade Inspection Drone (Larkspur; Leading Edge Tile Image). Substation: Export Cable Monitor (alarms→Control Engineer), Fire Detection Panel, Emergency Generator (Foxglove; auto start on aux loss; no unapproved paralleling; Start Test Trace→Substation Operator), Helideck. Modes: Substation Degraded, Grid Constraint, Weather Hold, Vessel Standby, Turbine Lockout (no remote restart during fire investigation). Fleet Dispatch Console (Sable Orchard). Alarms: safety>protection>export; not cleared on detector reset. SCADA Gateway (Juniper Vale; data→Shore Control Room; Session Revocation Receipt→Cybersecurity Gateway). Shore Control Room (Amber Quay; hub; holds last limit on grid comms loss). Maintenance Planning Engine (Thistle Crown; Squall Window Bulletin; Deferred Task Rationale). Operations Radio Console (voice to CTV, SOV, Daughter Craft). Personnel Tracking Console. Weather Analyst: Wave Burst Record; Visibility Confidence Note→Duty Planner. Marine Coordinator: Berth Slot Confirmation. Vessel Master: Transfer Manifest Addendum; Crew Count Correction→Personnel Tracking Console. Recovery Basket Load Sheet→Rescue Coordinator. HSE Officer: evacuation advice. Field Supervisor: work status→Shore Control Room. North Access Scanner: credential, authorization active for period/area; deny otherwise; gate secured if unverifiable; no verbal override; unique transaction ID. Southern route scanner: individual credential, owner match, area/time authorization; logs entries/denials timestamped; visual permit/deny indicator; barrier closed on failure; no holding barrier; anti-tailgating; visitors same checks; escort verified; signage; commissioning/routine checks; faults→out of service; approved alternative entry if unavailable; credential-free emergency egress; change control. East Service Lift: door-interlock and overload check before

New part:
S866: The hoist, suspension points, and visible cable sections are examined for wear, corrosion, or abnormal movement.
S867: The Electrical Technician verifies that the lift supply and protective devices show no active fault indication.
S868: The inspector confirms that the rated capacity and operating instructions remain legible at the car entrance.
S869: The Field Supervisor records the inspection result and any observed defects in the maintenance system.
S870: A defect affecting safe operation prevents release until the required repair and verification are complete.
S871: The Work Permit Portal is checked for active restrictions that could conflict with lift operation.
S872: The Duty Planner confirms that the planned work can proceed within the lift capacity and operating limits.
S873: Personnel are briefed on the permitted landings, maximum occupancy, and emergency actions before boarding.
S874: The Personnel Tracking Console is used to maintain an accurate record of personnel entering and leaving the route.
S875: Equipment is inspected for dimensions, mass, and secure packaging before it is accepted for transport.
S876: The Storekeeper confirms that equipment intended for the lift is ready and properly identified for the work party.
S877: Long or unstable loads are not carried unless an approved handling arrangement keeps the load contained within the car.
S878: The operator positions each load to avoid obstructing doors, controls, and emergency access.
S879: The Field Supervisor confirms that no person is exposed to a suspended or shifting load during movement.
S880: The release decision is based on a satisfactory inspection, valid work authorization, and compliance with stated limits.
S881: The Field Supervisor communicates the release status to the work party and records the time that service is authorized.
S882: During operation, users report unusual noise, vibration, door behavior, or control response immediately.
S883: The lift is removed from service if a new condition could compromise safe movement, pending assessment and corrective action.
S884: The West Service Lift provides vertical access along the west route between the designated service landings.
S885: Its use is limited to personnel and equipment authorized for the turbine work area.
S886: Before boarding, the Field Supervisor confirms that the work authorization covers the intended landing and task.
S887: The Field Supervisor also verifies that the landing is accessible and that the route is clear of obstructions.
S888: The operator checks the lift identification, rated capacity, and current service status before each operating period.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
